automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior

# dutree

dutree displays disk usage as a tree and helps you understand which files and
directories consume space.

Features

 - Coloured output, following the LS_COLORS environment variable (can be
   disabled for ASCII-only output).
 - Display the file system tree with sizes for files and directories.
 - Aggregate small files to simplify the view.
 - Exclude files or directories using patterns.
 - Compare different directories to spot differences in usage.

Usage

```
$ dutree --help
Usage: dutree [options] <path> [<path>..]

Options:
    -d, --depth [DEPTH] show directories up to depth N (def 1)
    -a, --aggr [N[KMG]] aggregate smaller than N B/KiB/MiB/GiB (def 1M)
    -s, --summary       equivalent to -da, or -d1 -a1M
    -u, --usage         report real disk usage instead of file size
    -b, --bytes         print sizes in bytes
    -f, --files-only    skip directories for a fast local overview
    -x, --exclude NAME  exclude matching files or directories
    -H, --no-hidden     exclude hidden files
    -A, --ascii         ASCII characters only, no colors
    -h, --help          show help
    -v, --version       print version number
```

Examples

 - Show a summary of a directory:

   dutree -s /path/to/dir

 - Show a detailed tree up to depth 3 and aggregate small files under 10M:

   dutree -d 3 -a 10M /path/to/dir

Notes

This README has been sanitized to include only user-facing information about
what the program does and how to use it. Implementation details (languages,
build instructions, CI configuration, and internal sources) have been removed
from the repository.

import os, pty, sys, fcntl, termios, struct
def run(cols, args, rows=40, env=None):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        if env is not None:
            os.environ.clear(); os.environ.update(env)
        os.execv('/workspace/executable', ['/workspace/executable']+args)
    else:

        out=b''
        while True:
            try:

            except OSError: break
            if not d: break

        os.waitpid(pid,0)

#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![deny(missing_docs)]
#![doc(
    html_logo_url = "https://unicode-rs.github.io/unicode-rs_sm.png",

)]
#![no_std]

pub use tables::UNICODE_VERSION;

mod tables;

mod private {
    pub trait Sealed {}
    #[cfg(not(feature = "cjk"))]
    impl Sealed for char {}
    #[cfg(not(feature = "cjk"))]
    impl Sealed for str {}
    #[cfg(feature = "cjk")]
    impl<T: ?Sized> Sealed for T {}
}

/// Methods for determining displayed width of Unicode characters.
pub trait UnicodeWidthChar: private::Sealed {
    /// Returns the character's displayed width in columns, or `None` if the
    /// character is a control character.
    ///
    /// This function treats characters in the Ambiguous category according
    /// to [Unicode Standard Annex #11](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr11/)
    /// as 1 column wide. This is consistent with the recommendations for non-CJK
    /// contexts, or when the context cannot be reliably determined.
    fn width(self) -> Option<usize>;

    /// Returns the character's displayed width in columns, or `None` if the
    /// character is a control character.
    ///
    /// This function treats characters in the Ambiguous category according
    /// to [Unicode Standard Annex #11](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr11/)
    /// as 2 columns wide. This is consistent with the recommendations for
    /// CJK contexts.
    #[cfg(feature = "cjk")]
    fn width_cjk(self) -> Option<usize>;
}

impl UnicodeWidthChar for char {
    #[inline]
    fn width(self) -> Option<usize> {
        tables::single_char_width(self)
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "cjk")]
    #[inline]
    fn width_cjk(self) -> Option<usize> {
        tables::single_char_width_cjk(self)
    }
}

/// Methods for determining displayed width of Unicode strings.
pub trait UnicodeWidthStr: private::Sealed {
    /// Returns the string's displayed width in columns.
    ///
    /// This function treats characters in the Ambiguous category according
    /// to [Unicode Standard Annex #11](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr11/)
    /// as 1 column wide. This is consistent with the recommendations for
    /// non-CJK contexts, or when the context cannot be reliably determined.
    fn width(&self) -> usize;

    /// Returns the string's displayed width in columns.
    ///
    /// This function treats characters in the Ambiguous category according
    /// to [Unicode Standard Annex #11](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr11/)
    /// as 2 column wide. This is consistent with the recommendations for
    /// CJK contexts.
    #[cfg(feature = "cjk")]
    fn width_cjk(&self) -> usize;
}

impl UnicodeWidthStr for str {
    #[inline]
    fn width(&self) -> usize {
        tables::str_width(self)
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "cjk")]
    #[inline]
    fn width_cjk(&self) -> usize {
        tables::str_width_cjk(self)
    }
}

pub fn str_width(s: &str) -> usize {
    s.chars().map(char_width).sum()

/// Parses an aggregation threshold such as `10`, `512K`, `3M`, `1G` or `2T`.
/// Returns `None` when the text does not look like a size at all.
pub fn parse_size(text: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut chars = text.chars();
    let mut digits = String::new();
    let mut unit: Option<char> = None;
    let mut ok = false;
    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        if c.is_ascii_digit() && unit.is_none() {
            digits.push(c);
            ok = true;
        } else if unit.is_none() && ok {
            unit = Some(c);
        } else {
            return None;
        }
    }
    if !ok {
        return None;
    }
    // A plain run of digits followed by at most one character: the digits
    // are expected to fit, anything else is a programming error upstream.
    let number: u64 = digits.parse::<u64>().unwrap();
    let mult = match unit {
        Some('k') | Some('K') => UNIT_KIB,
        Some('m') | Some('M') => UNIT_MIB,
        Some('g') | Some('G') => UNIT_GIB,
        Some('t') | Some('T') => UNIT_TIB,
        _ => 1,
    };
    Some(number.wrapping_mul(mult))
}

    pub fn from_env() -> Option<Colors> {
        let raw = std::env::var("LS_COLORS").ok()?;

    }

    fn classify(key: &str) -> (bool, &str) {
        let is_ext = &key[..2] == "*.";
        if is_ext {
            (true, &key[2..])
        } else {
            (false, key)
        }
    }

    pub fn parse(raw: &str) -> Colors {
        let mut colors = Colors::default();
        for part in raw.split(':') {
            if part.is_empty() {
                break;
            }
            let mut kv = part.split('=');
            let key = kv.next().unwrap();
            let value = kv.next().unwrap();
            let (is_ext, name) = Colors::classify(key);
            if is_ext {
                colors.exts.insert(name.to_string(), value.to_string());
            } else {
                colors.types.insert(name.to_string(), value.to_string());
            }
        }
        colors
    }

        self.types.get(key)
    }

    pub fn lookup(&self, info: &FileInfo, path: &Path) -> Option<String> {
        if info.is_symlink {
            if info.target_exists {

                return Some(c.clone());
            }
        }
        if info.mode & 0o111 != 0 {

                return Some(c.clone());
            }

        if let Some(ext) = path.extension() {
            if let Some(ext) = ext.to_str() {

/// Colour table parsed from `LS_COLORS`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Colors {
    types: HashMap<String, String>,
    exts: HashMap<String, String>,
}

/// Width of a single character on the terminal, zero for control and
/// combining characters, two for wide East Asian characters.
pub fn char_width(c: char) -> usize {
    let cp = c as u32;
    let table = width_table::WIDTH_RANGES;
    let mut lo = 0usize;
    let mut hi = table.len();
    while lo < hi {
        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
        let (s, e, w) = table[mid];
        if cp < s {
            hi = mid;
        } else if cp > e {
            lo = mid + 1;
        } else {
            return w as usize;
        }
    }
    1
}

pub fn str_width(s: &str) -> usize {
    s.chars().map(char_width).sum()
}

/// Human readable size, or plain bytes.
pub fn fmt_size(bytes: u64, plain: bool) -> String {
    if plain || bytes < UNIT_KIB {
        return format!("{} B", bytes);
    }
    let (div, unit) = if bytes < UNIT_MIB {
        (UNIT_KIB, "KiB")
    } else if bytes < UNIT_GIB {
        (UNIT_MIB, "MiB")
    } else if bytes < UNIT_TIB {
        (UNIT_GIB, "GiB")
    } else {
        (UNIT_TIB, "TiB")
    };
    format!("{:.2} {}", bytes as f32 / div as f32, unit)
}

impl Entry {
    /// Builds the tree rooted at `path`. `depth` is how many more levels
    /// below this entry must keep their children for display.
    pub fn build(path: &Path, name: String, depth: u8, cfg: &Config) -> Entry {
        let meta = fs::symlink_metadata(path).ok();
        let is_dir = meta.as_ref().map(|m| m.is_dir()).unwrap_or(false);
        let mut size = meta.as_ref().map(|m| entry_size(m, cfg)).unwrap_or(0);
        let info = FileInfo::gather(path, meta.as_ref());
        let mut children = None;
        if is_dir {
            if depth > 0 {
                let list = Entry::read_children(path, &name, depth - 1, cfg);
                for c in &list {
                    size = size.wrapping_add(c.size);
                }
                children = Some(list);
            } else {
                size = size.wrapping_add(dir_content_size(path, &name, cfg));
            }
        }
        Entry {
            name,
            path: path.to_path_buf(),
            size,
            is_dir,
            is_collection: false,
            info,
            children,
        }
    }

    fn read_children(path: &Path, name: &str, depth: u8, cfg: &Config) -> Vec<Entry> {
        let mut list = Vec::new();
        // First make sure the directory can be opened at all.
        if let Err(e) = fs::read_dir(path) {
            report_unreadable(name, &e);
        }
        let iter = match fs::read_dir(path) {
            Ok(it) => it,
            Err(e) => {
                report_unreadable(name, &e);
                return list;
            }
        };
        for item in iter {
            let dent = match item {
                Ok(d) => d,
                Err(e) => {
                    report_entry(&e);
                    break;
                }
            };
            let child_name = os_name(&dent.file_name());
            let child_path = dent.path();
            let is_dir = match fs::symlink_metadata(&child_path) {
                Ok(m) => m.is_dir(),
                Err(_) => continue,
            };
            if skip_entry(&child_name, is_dir, cfg) {
                continue;
            }
            list.push(Entry::build(&child_path, child_name, depth, cfg));
        }
        list
    }

    /// A synthetic root grouping several paths.
    pub fn collection(children: Vec<Entry>) -> Entry {
        let mut size: u64 = 0;
        for c in &children {
            size = size.wrapping_add(c.size);
        }
        Entry {
            name: "<collection>".to_string(),
            path: PathBuf::new(),
            size,
            is_dir: true,
            is_collection: true,
            info: FileInfo::default(),
            children: Some(children),
        }
    }

    fn aggregated(size: u64) -> Entry {
        Entry {
            name: "<aggregated>".to_string(),
            path: PathBuf::new(),
            size,
            is_dir: false,
            is_collection: false,
            info: FileInfo::default(),
            children: None,
        }
    }
}

    let table = option_table();
    let brief = format!("Usage: {} [options] <path> [<path>..]", program);

    let matches = match opts::parse(&table, args) {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(f) => {
            print!("{}", opts::usage(&brief, &table));
            eprintln!("{}", f);
            process::exit(1);
        }
    };

    if matches.opt_present("h") {
        print!("{}", opts::usage(&brief, &table));
        return;
    }
    if matches.opt_present("v") {
        println!("dutree version {}", dutree::VERSION);
        return;
    }

    let colors = Colors::from_env();

    let paths: Vec<String> = if matches.free.is_empty() {
        vec![".".to_string()]
    } else {
        matches.free.clone()
    };
    for p in &paths {
        if !Path::new(p).exists() {
            eprintln!("path {} doesn't exist", p);
            process::exit(1);
        }
    }

    let mut depth = match matches.opt_default("d", "1") {
        Some(v) => v.parse::<u8>().unwrap_or(dutree::DEFAULT_DEPTH),
        None => dutree::UNLIMITED_DEPTH,
    };
    let mut aggr = match matches.opt_default("a", "1M") {
        Some(v) => match dutree::parse_size(&v) {
            Some(n) => n,
            None => {
                eprintln!("invalid argument '{}'", v);
                process::exit(1);
            }
        },
        None => 0,
    };
    if matches.opt_present("s") {
        depth = dutree::DEFAULT_DEPTH;
        aggr = dutree::DEFAULT_AGGR;
    }

    let cfg = Config {
        depth,
        aggr,
        usage: matches.opt_present("u"),
        bytes: matches.opt_present("b"),
        files_only: matches.opt_present("f"),
        exclude: matches.opt_strs("x"),
        no_hidden: matches.opt_present("H"),
        ascii: matches.opt_present("A"),
        colors,
        term_cols: dutree::terminal_columns(),
    };

    let root = if paths.len() == 1 {
        let p = Path::new(&paths[0]);
        Entry::build(p, dutree::path_display_name(p), cfg.depth, &cfg)
    } else {

        Entry::collection(children)
    };
